title: KADMON VEIL — THE TITHE YARD
intro:
Forty square kilometres.

The Owed is ninety-one cycles of tithe, assembled to grade, sealed in vacuum
silos in ranks, each stack labelled with its cycle and its assessed value in
the hand of whichever Assessor was alive that year.

None of it has been opened. None of it has been eaten.

Rhod walks you along the first rank and recites the assessed value of each
stack from memory, in order, because he was examined on it at fourteen.
revisit: The Yard. Forty square kilometres of it, in ranks, by cycle.
look:
Ranks of vacuum silos to the horizon, labelled by cycle, in ninety-one
different hands.

The STACKS, sealed.
The SEALS, unbroken.
RHOD, reciting assessed values from memory.

objects.careless: Ninety-one cycles of assembled tithe in vacuum silos, in ranks, by year. It goes past the point where you can see the end of it.
objects.careful:
Cycle one is nearest the road, because the road was built to it, and cycle ninety-one is four kilometres out, because they kept going.

Processed protein, grain-husk, refined ore, and eleven silos of pharmaceutical precursor from the years when Erasmus still had the plant for it.

Rhod, at your elbow: "The Owed would feed this world for one year and four months, sir. That figure is in Report 415 and the Marchioness recalculates it every cycle."

"And nobody has opened it."

"It is assembled, sir." He is genuinely confused. "It is not ours. It has been assessed and it is awaiting collection."

A million and a half people a year, chiefly respiratory, for ninety-one years, walking past one year and four months of food that belongs to somebody who is not coming.

[ observed ]

objects.careless: Each stack carries a seal and a label: cycle, grade, assessed value, Assessor's mark.
objects.careful:
Ninety-one hands.

The early ones are on proper vellum in a formal chancery script. Around cycle nineteen the vellum stops and the labels go onto scraped stock, and the script changes with each Assessor and then changes again as each Assessor gets old.

Cycle sixty-seven is in a shaky hand that steadies over the next three cycles, which means somebody learned to write it while somebody else was dying.

The seals are unbroken. All of them. Forty square kilometres of unbroken seals, checked quarterly, in a hive that has been short of protein since year forty.

exits.text: West, back into the hive. Neither of you says anything for the first kilometre.

assessed and labelled and sealed and unopened.

It would feed this world for one year and four months. That figure is in Report
415 and she recalculates it every cycle, which means she has done the sum
ninety-one times and left the seals on.
